calibre-ebooks 1.0.12

- Added support for querying available formats for a specific book via API client.
- Updated documentation to include the new command for checking book formats.
- Internal code updates across API routes, services, models, and database layers to support format resolution and enhance maintainability.

- Added format conversion service for books (format_conversion_service.py).
- Updated API routes, database layer, main app, and models to support new features and improvements.
- Updated SQL optimization rules.
- Improved overall modularity and extensibility for book format handling.

- Added new agent documentation and configuration files in the rapport-bibliotecario-agent directory.
- Removed outdated skill-card.md file.
- Updated and reorganized SKILL.md documentation for clarity and accuracy.
- No changes to API interface or client functionality.

**Major update: Split and refactored the Calibre E-books gateway/server. Improved Python client with endpoint auto-discovery and dynamic mapping for robust API usage.**

- Server code moved from `calibre-openclaw-server` to the new `calibre-openclaw-gateway` directory.
- Many new gateway modules and endpoints added for books, downloads, embeddings, stats, web socket, and services.
- Python API client (`books_api_client.py`) now features dynamic endpoint discovery and argument mapping from OpenAPI, preventing hardcoding and improving robustness.
- Added new CLI commands: `find`, `download`, `cover`, `stats`, `status`, `upload` with dynamic mapping to API.
- Updated documentation to reflect the new gateway structure and enhanced dynamic API client.

- Added homepage URL to SKILL.md.
- Removed legacy skill-card.md file.
- Documentation updated in SKILL.md; no user-facing changes to API or major features.

- Introduced new services: added a virus scanning service and an ebook validator utility for enhanced file handling and validation.
- Updated multiple server and agent files for improved API integration and internal consistency.
- Documentation improvements in SKILL.md and agent docs.
- Removed obsolete documentation and markdown files to clean up the repo.

- Added dedicated semantic search (`semantic`) command to the API client, enabling direct RAG/content-based queries.
- Updated documentation for the Python API client with new command usage and clearer parameter explanations.
- Expanded and clarified search command: now performs catalog-first search with automatic semantic fallback when necessary.
- Added new "rapport-bibliotecario-agent" directory with agent metadata and configuration files.
- Removed deprecated `skill-card.md` file.

calibre-ebooks 1.0.5

- Removed 8 legacy files including server helpers, scripts, and documentation to streamline the skill.
- Updated core Python code in the Books API client and Postgres DB integration.
- Adjusted or removed tests related to content insights.
- No changes to primary user workflow; all documented commands, usage, and directory structure remain stable.
- Improved maintainability by cleaning up obsolete files and reducing code complexity.

- Major directory cleanup: 23 files removed, structure simplified and updated.
- Many server and service files changed; see repository for full details.
- Added initial test coverage with new test file.
- Documentation updated for clarity on API usage and directory structure.

- Synchronize and update server code, scripts, and configuration files across main and calibre-openclaw-server directories.
- Remove unused scripts/allow-docker-host-access.sh and skill-card.md for cleanup.
- Update and maintain parity between documentation and implementation, including SKILL.md.
- Refactor and update services and API routes for improved functionality and maintainability.
- Enhance examples and usage instructions for the Python Books API client.

- Refactored and reorganized project structure with parallel Calibre server and client code under calibre-openclaw-server.
- Improved Python API client, scripts, and helper tools for working with the Calibre Books API.
- Clarified and documented recommended directory usage for downloads, covers, and temporary artifacts.
- Removed deprecated skill-card.md.
- Updated and enhanced README and SKILL documentation for clearer usage and instructions.

calibre-ebooks v1.0.1

- Major file reorganization and cleanup across server and scripts.
- Removed obsolete files and duplicate documentation (`README copy.md`, old shell scripts, `skill-card.md`).
- Unified directory structure for server code, scripts, and temporary artifacts under `skills/calibre-ebooks/`.
- Revised and clarified SKILL.md usage documentation.
- Improved code consistency across API routes and helper scripts.

Initial release: Manage and query the local Calibre library via the Books API, with helpers for file and semantic RAG prep.

- Query and manage the Calibre library using the local Books API.
- Comprehensive documentation for API usage, endpoints, and helper scripts.
- Organized sandboxed directories for temporary files, covers, and downloads.
- Python API client included for command-line operations and automation.
- Prioritizes secure, local file handling and integration with Calibre library data.

- Added run-rag.sh script for new RAG operations and updated existing run.sh script.
- Improved API and embedding route handling and main server logic.
- Updated configuration, database access, and model definitions for better maintainability.
- Enhanced documentation with new README copy.
- General code and workflow improvements across embedding, conversion, and nightly tasks.

calibre-ebooks version 0.0.8

- Added `nightly_embeddings.py` for nightly embedding or indexing tasks.
- Updated Postgres database integration in `postgres_db.py`.
- Improved install script in `install_service.sh`.
- No user-facing workflow changes; primary workflow and API usage remain as documented.

# calibre-ebooks 0.0.7 Changelog

- Updated documentation in README.md and calibre-openclaw-server/README.md.
- No code or functional changes—documentation only.

- Added new API endpoints for stats and websocket functionality.
- Introduced a basic dashboard HTML for book catalog or API status view.
- Improved local fallback configuration with explicit environment variable/CLI options for Calibre metadata DB.
- Enhanced documentation for local fallbacks and explicitly updated operational guidance in SKILL.md.
- Updated response rules to include a precise answer regarding book source if asked.

calibre-ebooks v0.0.5

- Added Python scripts for Calibre metadata querying and document semantic RAG processing: `calibre_query.py`, `document_semantic_rag.py`, and requirements for RAG.
- Updated documentation to include detailed usage instructions for new local Python helpers and fallback options.
- No changes to primary API workflow—enhancements focus on robust local operations when API is unavailable or for semantic indexing.

Major update: Switched from direct Calibre DB/scripts to a local Books API as primary catalog/search interface, with new OpenAPI-driven workflow.

- Introduced calibre-openclaw-server: a local Books API server with OpenAPI support, codebase and docs added.
- Added a Node.js API client (books-api-client.mjs) for dynamic endpoint discovery and API access.
- SKILL.md and README.md rewritten to emphasize API-first search, metadata, and downloads—previous direct script usage is now fallback only.
- Removed legacy direct Python scripts and requirements related to Calibre/query/RAG from default workflow.
- New metadata key specifies external binary (node, python3) requirements.
- Response and workflow guidance updated for explicit API-first, OpenAPI-driven interaction, with local Calibre scripts only as last resort.

- Added instructions for using the new --convert-all option in document_semantic_rag.py to index all supported documents in a folder.
- Updated example CLI commands to include --convert-all usage.
- No changes to functionality—documentation clarification and enhancement only.

- Expanded and clarified the skill documentation, covering Calibre library operations, recommended workflows, and RAG integration.
- Outlined usage of calibredb and Python scripts for read-only metadata queries, exporting, conversion, and semantic search.
- Added explicit command examples for listing, searching, exporting, and metadata inspection.
- Documented fallback behaviors, requirements, and user response guidelines to ensure reliability and transparency.
- Provided detailed instructions for semantic RAG indexing, searching, and managing dependencies.
